newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian court denies former premier Rao's bail plea.
newsitem.headline: Indian court denies former premier Rao's bail plea.

text.p: An Indian court on Thursday denied a request by former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao for legal protection against arrest in a criminal conspiracy case, court officials said.
The Delhi High Court rejected Rao's request for anticipatory bail in the $100,000 case, they said. Anticipatory bail protects an accused against arrest.
"The application is not maintainable," S.K. Mahajan, a judge, said while dismissing Rao's plea.
Rao's lawyer on Wednesday asked for anticipatory bail ahead of a hearing next Monday in the $100,000 cheating case.
Rao resigned as president of the Congress party on Saturday after a judge ordered him to obey a summons to appear in court as a co-accused at Monday's hearing.

Indian expatriate businessman Lakhubhai Pathak alleges that Rao and a Hindu guru conspired to cheat him of $100,000 in 1983. Rao has said he is innocent. The two other accused, guru Chandraswami and his assistant, are in jail.
